published.source: tradeshallglasgow.co.uk/rooms (research/research-room-facts.md, fetched 2026-10-17); the venue's own room plan labels 9.6 m, 7.3 m and 12 m
published.note: Measured: an L of 101.8 m2. Window part 9.60-9.63 m wide (9.449 m of window wall between the west wall and the north-east pier) by 5.890 m (west) to 6.066 m (east); inner part 7.266 m wide by 6.510 m (to the south wall's west plane) or 6.005 m (east plane); 12.400 m from the window wall to the wardrobe doors on the west, 12.071 m on the east. Ceilings 3.126 m (window part), 2.82 m (two coffers), 2.419 m and 2.514 m (soffits). Drawing and planning use the measured outline; the published capacities are kept (decided 18 October 2026).

source.note: Capture date as the twin gives it; unverified, as the Saloon's config notes.

transform.note: x = X - 16.06, y = Z + 2.869, z = 7.36 - Y. A proper rotation (det +1); the window wall is on -z (z = -6.202) and +x points 11.1 deg true. The centre is the middle of the outline's bounding box (X 11.227..20.893, Y 1.162..13.562) within 2 mm. Floor Z -2.869 is the floor plane at the centre (-2.8690 by the area-weighted fit, -2.8685 by plumb lines); the floor is not level, see floor.note.

site.note: Derived from the Grand Hall frame constants (tools/grand-hall-survey/README.md, Frame; merchant-city-v2 frame block), as the Saloon's. This room's planner -z is E57 +Y, opposite the Grand Hall's -z (E57 -Y, 101.1 deg true, 102.96 grid): 281.1 true, 282.96 grid. gridOrigin = the Grand Hall's (259332, 665191) + this origin's Grand Hall planner position (x = 8.795 - 16.06 = -7.265, z = 7.36 + 4.963 = 12.323) on +x (-0.22427, -0.97453) and +z (-0.97453, 0.22427) = (259332 + 1.629 - 12.009, 665191 + 7.080 + 2.764). floorODN = 14.19 - 0.045 - 2.869 (the Grand Hall's floor is E57 Z 0.045 at 14.19 m ODN); pavementY = 10.40 - 11.276, the Glassford Street pavement, which this room does not face. The windows look west-north-west over the rear yard: its ground level, the rear facade's line and the skylines are not measured here (the 17 October research puts the yard at about E57 Z -3.3, y -0.43: a lead, unverified).

segments.note: E57 Y = 13.562, facing 281.1 deg true. The bare face is seen only at the west end (X 11.26..11.60, 0.33 m per level, rms 0.8 mm; a tape line from the stub wall there gives 13.561). Its direction is NOT measured: it is drawn parallel to the E57 X axis. The pelmet over the curtains (soffit 2.89 m) is not parallel to that axis: its face is 0.21 m in front of Y 13.56 at X 11.45 and 0.30 m at X 20.45 (-0.57 deg, a straight line), and the drapes' fronts drift the same way by 4 cm. If the wall is parallel to its pelmet, its east end is at Y 13.47, 9 cm nearer the room than drawn, and the glass depths below shrink or grow with it. Sheers and drapes hang 0.14-0.18 m in front of the wall from a track under the pelmet to the floor. Skirting line Y 13.545 at the west end.

floor.note: Dark, glossy hardwood strip boards running along E57 Y (planner z), about 0.13 m wide (read off one floor crop, not measured). Not level: the floor rises towards the windows, Z = -2.8999 + 0.00075 X + 0.00251 Y (area-weighted, rms 6.5 mm) or -2.9161 + 0.00123 X + 0.00378 Y (plumb lines, rms 9 mm), 3-5 cm over the room's length, while the ceilings are level; clear heights under the window part's field run 3.08-3.14 m. The gloss mirrors every downlight: floor photographs need glare handling.

freeStanding.note: White, square, with a moulded base (settled from the cube faces: not round). Faces E57 X 14.657/14.942, Y 7.072/7.351 (rms 3.0-6.8 mm).
Faces E57 X 14.634/14.901, Y 2.813/3.119 (rms 1.2-5.2 mm); under the edge between the soffit and the south band.

concealedLights.note: An LED strip on the picture rail washes the band above it on every wall but the window wall (2.13 m to the soffit in the inner part, to the cornice in the window part). The coffers' rims hold a second concealed uplight, which the schema cannot place (it lists walls only).

edits.note: PROPOSED. The corridor door stood open: a plain recess, its closed leaf modelled by the web. Leaf plane not measured.

provenance.method: As the Saloon's: plan sections of the reviewed Matterport dollhouse mesh with robust line fits (RANSAC then Tukey IRLS) in three height bands; 2 cm orthographic depth rasters of each wall for openings; the lowest down-facing surface on a 2.5 cm raster for the ceiling. An independent pass by ray casting (tape lines wall to wall, fans of rays from the 22 stations, plumb lines on a 0.2 m grid) checked the outline and the heights. The windows, which the mesh does not hold, were read from the native E57 cube faces (4096 px) re-projected on planes parallel to the wall and compared between stations. residuals.note: By eye the head and sill lines keep their height on the plane Y 13.80 between stations 1.9 m and 3.8-5.0 m away (1 cm of reading is 4 cm of depth). An automatic reading (07_window_edges.py heads) has the second window's head at 2.609-2.624 m from five stations 1.9 to 4.5 m away, so that frame is within about 2 cm of Y 13.80; on the other three it scatters by 7-50 mm between stations and would put the frames 0.03-0.12 m further back; not resolved. The window wall's unmeasured direction adds up to 9 cm at the east end.

Through a sheer, 2.5-4 mm crops; the head reads 2.54-2.62 m by eye over the four windows and 2.56, 2.61, 2.59 and 2.57 m automatically (it may differ from window to window), and up to 2.65 m if the frames lie further back.
